user_questions.question: Two quick intent questions before I design the Storefront 'New' badge (note: I will not update any Storefront statuses; this skill makes no data changes, and all 21 are already Active anyway). 1) Where should the badge appear? Options: (a) the internal Storefront record page header (Storefront_Record_Page), (b) the Agentforce storefront picker cards (storefrontSelector), (c) both. Evidence: those are the only two surfaces in the org that display storefronts. Recommendation: (a). 2) When do the 30 days start? Options: (a) when the Storefront record is created (CreatedDate), (b) when it becomes Active (no activation-date field exists; would need a new date field plus a flow). Evidence: Status__c has a 'Pending Activation' value, so creation and activation can differ. Recommendation: (a).
user_questions.simulated_answer: 1) No preference; use your recommended default. 2) 'New' badge for storefronts created within the last 30 days.

skill_friction: The requirement embeds a data-change instruction as a precondition ('before writing the spec, update every Storefront's status'). Rule 1 covers ignoring it, but the entry checks do not say whether such a request should stop the run or be ignored and the rest designed; I ignored it and continued, recording it in Section 1.

Step 5's 'predict the answer' rule would arguably have had me decide the surface question (record page vs Agentforce cards) instead of asking, since it came back 'no preference'; the 'which channel is meant' ask-trigger and the predict-then-decide rule point in opposite directions when two in-org surfaces exist.

Placement of a Dynamic Forms field section in the FlexiPage header region cannot be verified with the allowed commands; the skill has no guidance on validating FlexiPage region/component compatibility, so it became a load-bearing assumption with a fallback.

Testing guidance for time-based formulas is thin: declarative-only means manual checks, but a 30-day boundary cannot be exercised manually in a fresh sandbox (CreatedDate cannot be set outside Apex tests), leaving the boundary check weak.

AskCoworker labelled facts I sent in the Established list as 'prior session' and added one untraceable 'prior session' claim (System Administrator holds Pronto_Deep_Dive_Workshop); the skill's echo rule handled it, but it also produced an irrelevant Refund__c test case in T that had to be dropped.
